games.title: Scourge Survivors
games.blurb: First-person horde-survivors — Vampire Survivors x DOOM.
games.courseAngle: Flagship proof for scoped slicing, runtime assets, HUD polish, and E2E playability.
games.summary: A brutal first-person survivor run inside the Deadrot war: hold the breach, burn back the Scourge, and fight room to room through multi-storey ruins. The studio's first finished case study, start to summary.
proofPoints: Complete run loop: menu, death summary, restart, victory summary
3D animated Scourge and full weapon viewmodels — idle, fire, reload, jump
Multi-level arenas with stairs, openable doors and windows, enterable buildings
Desktop and mobile E2E journeys over real play, no unexpected console errors

games.title: Deadlane
games.blurb: 3D tower defense — hold the line for the Wardens.
games.courseAngle: Shows how to turn a tiny grid prototype into a readable tower-defense loop.
games.summary: A lane-defense pressure cooker for the Wardens: place defenses, manage economy, survive the wave, and make the front line legible.
proofPoints: Grid, pathfinding, towers, waves, and economy
Clear build/fight/fail/restart loop
Asset and E2E gates before finished status

games.title: Pactfall
games.blurb: Pyre-vs-Wardens MOBA built around the Pact.
games.courseAngle: The disciplined-scope example: lane/champion fantasy without letting PvP swallow v1.
games.summary: The Pact starts breaking in the lanes. Pactfall owns champion, objective, and jungle pressure so Starblight can stay orbital.
proofPoints: Champion/ability model with constrained v1 scope
Lane objective and Scourge pressure
Multiplayer deferred until offline/local loop is finished

games.title: Starblight
games.blurb: Arcade pilot shooter against the orbital infection.
games.courseAngle: A board-hygiene case study: lock the genre, cut MOBA drift, finish the run loop.
games.summary: A momentum-heavy orbital shooter where pilots carve through Scourge infection above the planet instead of getting dragged into lane/MOBA scope.
proofPoints: Orbital shooter direction locked on the Deadrot board
MOBA/lane scope deferred into Pactfall/Bloodlane
Flight, combat, boss, and E2E completion gates

games.title: Redline
games.blurb: High-speed courier runner through a burning Deadrot route.
games.courseAngle: A compact proof for feel tuning, speed readability, checkpoints, and juice.
games.summary: A Pyre courier run built around speed, hazards, checkpoints, and the moment a prototype becomes something players can actually finish.
proofPoints: One complete course with fail/finish/restart
Speed, hazard, checkpoint, and crash feedback
Desktop/mobile journey before finished status

games.title: Rothulk
games.blurb: Side-scrolling infiltration inside a living Scourge bio-ship.
games.courseAngle: The platformer-feel case study: movement, collision, hazards, and one finished level.
games.summary: A bio-ship infiltration platformer where the first job is not a huge campaign; it is one nasty level that feels finished.
proofPoints: Traversal, hazard, HP, and ignite loop
One complete level before campaign scope
Platform feel checked across desktop and mobile

games.title: Warline
games.blurb: Persistent strategy front for the Deadrot war.
games.courseAngle: The meta-layer proof: operation contracts, live/fallback state, and product framing.
games.summary: The persistent war board tying the browser games together: hold lanes, spend resources, read the front, and make Deadrot feel like one war.
proofPoints: Strategy front loop with visible operation feedback
Offline/live mode clarity
Catalog and E2E parity with the game apps
